statements.t: (Enbridge or the Company) (TSX:ENB) (NYSE:ENB) today reported third quarter 2026 financial results, reaffirmed its 2026 financial guidance and provided a quarterly business update.

Announced the US$2.6 billion acquisition of Tallgrass Energy LP's crude oil business (Tallgrass), which will expand the Company's Liquids Pipelines footprint to include a competitive Rockies-to-Cushing platform, and the US$0.3 billion Pony Express 2 (PXP2) growth project
Our secured growth backlog stands at $38 billion, even as we placed $3 billion of completed projects into service this quarter.
We've consistently added new projects to our backlog this year, positioning us well to deliver on our $10–20 billion target for new project announcements through 2027.
This acquisition is expected to provide us with a new corridor through the U.S.
We also sanctioned the Long Lake Expansion within our Alberta Regional Oil Sands business, with an expected in-service date of 2028.
This quarter we placed two projects into service, Tennessee Ridgeline and B.C.
The team is focused on executing our $15 billion portfolio of sanctioned projects across the continent, including the $4 billion Sunrise expansion of the B.C.
Our focus remains on executing our secured backlog and extending visibility to our 5% growth outlook.

We remain on track to achieve our financial guidance for the 21st consecutive year, reinforcing Enbridge’s ability to perform across varying macro-economic conditions and our first-choice investment proposition.

In the last four years we have been able to profitably grow Enbridge’s position in both Canada and the United States and secure an impressive backlog of growth projects across the company that will continue to fuel Enbridge’s growth and investor returns for years to come.
The Company reaffirms its 2026 financial guidance for adjusted EBITDA between $20.2 billion and $20.8 billion and DCF per share between $5.70 and $6.10.
The Company also reaffirms its medium-term outlook for adjusted EBITDA, DCF per share, and EPS average compound annual growth rate of approximately 5%.

The Company's rolling 12-month Debt-to-EBITDA metric at the end of the third quarter of 2026 was 5.1x, slightly above the target range due to the period end debt balance translating at a 1.42 CAD/USD foreign exchange rate compared to EBITDA translating at an average trailing 12-month rate of 1.39.

In developing estimates of fair values at the acquisition date, we utilize a variety of factors including market data, historical and future expected cash flows, growth rates and discount rates.
The subjective nature of our assumptions increases the risk associated with estimates surrounding the projected performance of the acquired entity.

Our evaluation includes, but is not limited to, the assessment of macroeconomic trends (including the impact of changes in discount rates and rate base multiple), changes to regulatory environments, capital accessibility, operating income trends (including changes to projected cash flows from operations, expected future capital expenditures and forecasted rate base), and changes to industry conditions.
If it is determined that the carrying value of an asset exceeds its expected undiscounted cash flows, we will assess the fair value of the asset.

We classify assets as held for sale when management commits to a formal plan to actively market an asset or a group of assets and when management believes it is probable the sale of the assets will occur within one year.

To recognize the economic effects of the actions of the regulator, the timing of recognition of certain revenues and expenses in these operations may differ from that otherwise expected under US GAAP for non-rate-regulated entities.
The rates for a number of our projects are based on a cost-of-service recovery model that follows the regulators' authoritative guidance.
Under the cost-of-service tolling methodology, we calculate tolls based on forecast volumes and cost.

If there are changes in our assessment of the probability of recovery for a regulatory asset, we reduce its carrying amount to the balance that we expect to recover from customers in future periods through rates.

We determine discount rates by reference to rates of high-quality long-term corporate bonds with maturities that approximate the timing of future payments anticipated to be made under each of the respective plans.
